verses.1: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt, those dwelling in Migdol and in Tahpanhes and in Noph and in the land of Pathros, saying:
verses.2: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You have seen all the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. Behold, they are in ruins today, and there is no one living in them.
verses.3: Because of the evil they did to provoke me, going to burn incense to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors had known.
verses.4: I sent all my servants the prophets to them, early and late, saying, Do not do this abhorrent thing that I hate.
verses.5: Yet they did not listen and did not incline their ears to turn from their evil to stop burning incense to other gods.
verses.6: My anger and wrath burned in the cities of Judah and the outskirts of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as today.
verses.7: Now therefore, thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing such great evil to your own lives, cutting off from yourselves every man, woman, infant, and suckling from Judah, so that no remnant is left?
verses.8: To provoke me with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to dwell, in order to cut yourselves off and become a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth.
verses.9: Have you forgotten the evils of your ancestors and the evils of the kings of Judah and the evils of their wives, and your own evils and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and the outskirts of Jerusalem?
verses.10: They have not been humbled until this day, and they have not feared, and they have not walked in my teaching or in my statutes, which I set before you and before your ancestors.
verses.11: Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: I am setting my face against you for evil and to cut off all Judah.
verses.12: I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to dwell there. They will all fall by the sword and by famine, from the least to the greatest. They will die by the sword and by famine, and they will become an object of horror, a curse, and a disgrace.
verses.13: I will bring judgment upon those dwelling in the land of Egypt, just as I brought judgment upon Jerusalem, by the sword, by famine, and by plague.
verses.14: No fugitive and no remnant will be left among the remnant of Judah who have come to dwell there in the land of Egypt and to return to the land of Judah, which they are longing in their hearts to return to. They will not return, except the fugitives.
verses.15: Then all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods, and all the women standing in a great assembly and all the people dwelling in the land of Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah,
verses.16: The word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you.
verses.17: For we will do all the word that comes out of our mouths, to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drinks to her, just as we and our ancestors, our kings and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and the outskirts of Jerusalem. We were full of bread and had well-being, and we saw no evil.
verses.18: But since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drinks to her, we have been in famine and perished.
verses.19: And are we burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drinks to her without our husbands doing it for us and making figurines for her and pouring out drinks to her?
verses.20: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women, and to all the people answering him with these words,
verses.21: Has the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and the outskirts of Jerusalem, you and your ancestors, your kings and your rulers and the people of the land—has the LORD not remembered it and brought it to mind?
verses.22: And the LORD could no longer bear the evil of your deeds and the abominations you have done. Your land has become a ruin and a desolation and a curse, with no one living in it, as today.
verses.23: Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice, and did not walk in his teaching, his statutes, or his testimonies. Therefore this evil has befallen you today.
verses.24: Then Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
verses.25: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying, We will do the vows we have vowed to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drinks to her. Fulfill your vows and do what you have vowed.
verses.26: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all Judah living in the land of Egypt. I swear by my great name, says the LORD, that my name will no longer be invoked by any Judahite saying, The LORD lives, in all the land of Egypt.
verses.27: I am watching over them for evil and not for good. All the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will perish by the sword and by famine until they are finished.
verses.28: The few who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. Then the remnant of Judah who have gone to dwell in the land of Egypt will know whose word remains.
verses.29: And this is the sign for you, says the LORD, that I will bring judgment upon you, so that you may know that my words will rise against you for evil.
verses.30: Thus says the LORD: I will give Pharaoh Hophra, the king of Egypt, into the hands of his enemies and into the hands of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah, the king of Judah, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, his enemy and the one seeking his life.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "the Queen of Heaven" is a rendering of "מַלְכֶּת הַשָּׁמַיִם" (malket hashamayim), a title for a Canaanite goddess (likely Astarte or Ishtar), commonly referred to in this context in Jeremiah.
- v. 19: "making figurines for her" (כַּוָּנִים) is a reference to small idols or incense altars, which were part of the ritual practice of worshiping foreign deities.
